Inference benchmarking is the systematic process of measuring the performance of a trained machine learning model when it is deployed to make predictions on new, unseen data. ### 2. Why is it important to distinguish between latency and throughput?
Latency refers to the time it takes for a single request to be processed and returned to the user, which is critical for real-time applications like chatbots. A system might have high throughput by batching requests, but this often increases the latency for individual users.

Time to First Token (TTFT) measures the duration between the moment a user sends a prompt and the moment the model generates the very first character of the response. Tokens Per Second is calculated by dividing the total number of generated output tokens by the total time taken to generate them, excluding the initial prefill phase. The prefill phase occurs when the model processes the entire input prompt to create the initial KV cache, which is computationally intensive but highly parallelizable. Increasing the batch size allows the GPU to process multiple requests simultaneously, which significantly increases overall throughput by utilizing more of the hardware's parallel processing power. Quantization reduces the precision of model weights (e.g., from FP16 to INT8 or INT4), which shrinks the model's memory footprint and speeds up computation.
